subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A graphic 'grid' is used to...
options: Organise and align text and images consistently
questions.explain: A grid provides an underlying structure that keeps elements aligned and the layout consistent.

questions.q: Which of these is a natural fibre?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural plant fibre, while polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic.

questions.q: 'Smocking' is a technique that...
options: Gathers fabric with stitches to create decorative texture and stretch
questions.explain: Smocking gathers and stitches fabric to make a flexible, decoratively textured surface.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Colours that sit next to each other
Different tones of the same hue
Colours that sit directly opposite each other
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

questions.q: Appliqué is a technique that involves...
options: Stitching shaped pieces of fabric onto a larger background cloth
questions.explain: Appliqué sews cut pieces of fabric onto a background to build up an image or pattern.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.

questions.q: A wide aperture (low f-number) produces what kind of depth of field?
options: A shallow depth of field with a blurred background
Total blur across the whole image
A deep depth of field with everything sharp
questions.explain: A wide aperture gives a shallow depth of field, keeping the subject sharp while blurring the background.

questions.q: What is 'typography' in graphic design?
options: The art of arranging type and lettering
questions.explain: Typography is the design and arrangement of type so that text is legible and appealing.

questions.q: What does the 'white balance' setting on a camera adjust?
options: The colour cast so whites appear neutral under different lighting
questions.explain: White balance corrects colour casts so that whites look neutral under different light sources.

questions.q: Felting makes fabric by...
options: Matting and pressing fibres together with moisture and friction
questions.explain: Felting binds loose fibres into a fabric by pressing them with moisture, heat and friction.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: Increasing the 'contrast' of a photo does what?
options: Makes darks darker and lights lighter
questions.explain: Increasing contrast widens the difference between the lightest and darkest tones.

questions.q: Considering the 'cultural context' of an artwork means thinking about...
options: The time, place and society in which it was made
Just the size of the canvas
questions.explain: Cultural context considers the historical period, place and society that shaped the artwork.

questions.q: A 'raster' (bitmap) image is made up of...
questions.explain: Raster images are built from a grid of pixels, so enlarging them too far makes them look blocky.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

questions.q: Embroidery is best described as...
questions.explain: Embroidery decorates fabric using needle and thread to create stitched designs.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Write an essay with no images
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

questions.q: Abstract Expressionism is characterised by...
questions.explain: Abstract Expressionism used large-scale, energetic, often non-figurative gestural marks.

questions.q: The CMYK colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, key/black) is the standard ink set used in colour printing.

questions.q: 'Hierarchy' in a layout means...
options: Arranging elements so the most important information stands out first
questions.explain: Visual hierarchy uses size, weight and position to guide the eye to the most important content first.

questions.q: Joining materials together to make a 3D form is called...
questions.explain: Construction (or assembly) builds a 3D form by joining separate pieces together.
